Storage and recovery workshop

Unit 1 · Week 9 · Lesson 4 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the design chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Legacy console practice. These slides are not the current Pygame Task 1. Use the aligned game chapter and workbook. Replacement project slides are pending (A06).

1. Storage and recovery workshop

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Save accepted orders and preserve earlier records. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

2. Retrieval and explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval, then partner comparison

Append retains earlier file text. Follow the project contract: successful saving precedes adding the accepted order to the session list. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

3. Storage checks

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and teacher explanation

Use only disposable synthetic files. Check the agreed CSV fields and record separator in the starter. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

4. Two runs, two records

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, model and explain

With the agreed newline format, append gives two records. Opening in w truncates existing contents. Demonstrate only in a disposable folder. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

5. A failed save

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

It should remain unchanged under this project contract. Do not claim success or create a summary entry for an unsaved order. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

6. Independent practice

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application with optional support

Use a stub returning False or the supplied controlled failure fixture. Do not change OS permissions on important files. Check before/after session state and file contents. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

7. A choice to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Whole-class response and justification

A addresses the reported storage failure. Verify a correction with two runs rather than changing unrelated interface behaviour. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

8. Exit explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual reflection and fresh explanation

Expected: both valid records remain and a failed save does not falsely enter session data. Unfinished work becomes a specific next action. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#design. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.
